messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autopager fired for host gpu-host-342 — kubelet NotReady + host-heartbeat lost. Priority: P1. Pager: pagerduty, escalation policy: oncall-eng.

alice: acked. I'm on it. grabbing node details.

alice: `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu-host-342` shows `NotReady` state, 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff were on that node.

ben: @alice any customer-facing pods on that node?

alice: quick check — one inference deployment (redwood/generate-prod-v2) had 4 replicas, 1 replica on this node. Traffic should be automatically routed but metric spike in 5xxs for that route.

mira: seeing increased 5xx rate for /v1/generate (~3x) starting 2m ago. Dashboards: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/latency?node=gpu-host-342

caroline: paging history shows host lost serial heartbeat before kubelet flapped. suspect kernel-level failure.

alice: pulling serial console logs now. attaching snippet:``` dmesg | tail -n 50 
[ 1234.567890] NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 23s!
[ 1234.567895] kernel panic - not syncing: watchdog: BUG: see https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-panic
[ 1234.567900] CPU: 3 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/3 Not tainted 5.15.0-rt
```

ben: ugh. that looks like a kernel panic. Is autopsy showing GPU driver XID errors?

mira: also seeing NVidia Xid 79 entries just before panic in syslog.

alice: started cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-342` — node is already NotReady so cordon may not apply.

alice: drain won't work; kubelet NotReady, pods not evicting. Trying to force-evict with `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0` for the ones blocking scheduling.

caroline: paging info: pagerduty escalated to ben@redwood after 2 mins, then to caroline@redwood.

pagerduty: Escalation notice: Incident assigned to ben. Incident key: PD-6187654321.

ben: taking lead. I'm going to isolate the rack, open serial console full log, and start RMA plan if node is unrecoverable.

mira: customer impact estimate: approx 7% of active hosted inference requests routed to that AZ pool; fallback routing reduced impact to ~1.5% after autoscaling reroute kicked in. Still seeing 502/503 for some sessions.

alice: rolling temporary routing change to divert new sessions from that host's placement group. Pushing change to routing service:``` curl -XPOST https://controlplane/routing/override -d '{"avoid_node":"gpu-host-342","reason":"kubelet NotReady"}' ```

caroline: thumbs-up on the reroute. Also flagging for SRE to cross-check KV cache invalidation for affected sessions.

ben: dispatching hardware team to rack. If they confirm kernel-level failure, we'll follow RMA flow in runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hardware-rma.

incident-bot: Note: autopager auto-acked by alice at 6187654330.

alice: quick healthcheck on other nodes in same rack — two other GPU hosts show elevated CUDA driver errors but still responsive. schedule rolling node health checks.

mira: metrics: request latency for generate-prod-v2 spiked to 2.1s p95 for 6 minutes, error rate peaked at 8% then settled to 0.9% after reroute. Logging indicates 30 sessions had transient dropped connections.

caroline: Customer comms: do we need to open a status update? Affected customers likely on trial accounts; but this hit a small enterprise customer (acme-inc) with lower redundancy. Recommend short status note.

ben: agree. I'll draft a short incident email and hand to comms. tagging @oncall-rotation to prepare notice: `ACME INC — GPU host failure causing transient 5xx for some requests in us-west-2. Mitigated by rerouting; ongoing hardware investigation.`

alice: starting handoff — I'm going offline in 10m, ben will continue. leaving this thread with steps taken and logs.

alice: summary of steps: 1) acknowledged alert 2) checked serial logs (kernel panic) 3) attempted cordon/drain (kubelet NotReady) 4) force-deleted blocking pods 5) initiated routing override 6) notified hardware.

ben: thanks. I have PD control. I'll coordinate hardware, confirm RMA if needed, and update this thread. Taking over on-call.

mira: adding a follow-up: we should add a temporary health-check to preemptively fail nodes showing Xid79 spikes to avoid customer impact. filing a ticket: https://issues.redwood/OPS-9142

pagerduty: Incident note: ben acknowledged at 6187654352.

caroline: good job team. once hardware confirms, runbook suggests marking node as decommissioned if repeated kernel panics in last 72h.

ben: noted. setting reminder to update runbook entry with kernel panic signature and serial console snippet.

incident-bot: incident closed? not yet — waiting for hardware confirmation. If node goes back to Ready and passes health checks, auto-close; otherwise manual close after RMA.

alice: :thumbsup: I'll monitor logs for 15 more mins before I sign off.

ben: will post next update in 20.

mira: FYI — snapshot of prometheus query for error rate:```promql
sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (cluster)```

caroline: adding note: update incident severity to SEV2 if impact persists >30m.

ben: handoff complete. I have control and will escalate to hardware if they don't respond within 15m.

pagerduty: Escalation log: hardware-team paged at 6187654365.

incident-bot: thread annotated with runbook link and metrics snapshot.

ben: closing loop for now — mitigation in place, customer impact limited, hardware en route. will re-open if node recovers unpredictably. :white_check_mark:
